about: Trigger eval queries for this skill's description. A query is labelled with whether the skill should activate for it; the negatives are near-misses that share vocabulary with the skill but need something else. Split fixed so successive description edits are compared on the same ground: tune against train, judge against validation. Near-misses hardened 2026-09-16 after a measured 3-sample blind-router baseline scored this set 20/20: a set at the ceiling cannot register a loss when its description is edited, so negatives no router would have reached were replaced with ones a sibling skill owns. One hardened negative was withdrawn after that run: `does this PR introduce anything unsafe` fired 3/3 and the label, not the router, was wrong -- the description licenses a caller-stated scope, and a PR is one. Its slot now tests the `not code review` clause instead, on the quality-plus-security shape agent-ellis measurably wins.
how_to_run: `make eval` is the committed runner, but it covers only the queries a 3-sample blind-router baseline actually missed, not this whole file -- see CLAUDE.md for why 13 and not 380. To judge the rest: `skillgrade` runs a labelled set like this one and exits non-zero when the pass rate falls below a threshold. Needing nothing installed: run each query with `claude -p --output-format json` and count the runs whose transcript contains a Skill tool_use naming this skill. Cheapest of all, and closest to the router's real conditions: give a model only the name and description of every installed skill, with no bodies and no repo access, and have it pick one skill or none per query. `claude plugin eval`, which `make eval` drives, is generally available rather than early access; what it needs instead is a credential, a network and real money -- $0.142 a run, measured -- which is why it sits outside `make test` and CI does not run it. It will not reproduce this file query-for-query either: a bare query does not fire a skill, so a case is one of these queries rewritten as a realistic turn. This file stays the cheap, free, offline record.

queries.query: is there anything insecure anywhere in this codebase
do a security pass over the whole repo, not just my branch
we're filling in a vendor security questionnaire, find our weak spots
any injection or broken-auth bugs in here
map whatever security issues you find to CWE ids
i inherited this codebase, how bad is the security
